clue.text: Cleaner, very French, where there's a Gothic cathedral

parts.note: a char, or charwoman, is a British term for a cleaning lady
tres is the French word for very

explanation.surface: A tourist note pairing a cleaner and a French intensifier with a famous cathedral city.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAR is old British slang for a cleaning woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The French city southwest of Paris is famous for its Gothic cathedral of Notre-Dame.

clue.text: Legendary knight's weapon, auction item

parts.note: a lance is a long spear used by mounted knights
each item offered at an auction is a lot

explanation.surface: A legendary knight's weapon turns up for sale at auction.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Lancelot is the most famous of King Arthur's Round Table knights in legend.

clue.text: The Parisian, good sort, wasted chance

parts.note: le is the French masculine word for the, as said in Paris
toff is old informal slang for a decent fellow or a good sort

explanation.surface: A Parisian gentleman squanders an opportunity.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a let-off is a dropped catch or missed run-out that reprieves the batsman: a chance the fielding side wasted.
explanation.definitionFit: An escape or reprieve that comes from an opponent failing to take an opportunity is described that way.

clue.text: Where one may see M. Caine performing?

definitions.text: Where one may see M. Caine performing?

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters of the name doing an act, moving about into a new order

explanation.surface: Wondering where one might watch the actor Michael Caine act.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of M CAINE are rearranged, and the whole clue also defines the place where his films are shown.
explanation.definitionFit: Films starring Michael Caine are watched at a picture house, so that is where you would see him act.

clue.text: I agree to listen to judge

parts.note: to hear something is to listen to it
a judge hears a case in court, so to hear is to judge

explanation.surface: Someone agreeing to listen to a judge's ruling.
explanation.walkthrough: Two words of the same spelling come from different senses: listening and trying a case.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a cry of approval, as in parliamentary debate, voicing agreement with a speaker.

clue.text: Article, at that time, on a Greek goddess

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
then means at that time

explanation.surface: A written article, from a particular time, about a Greek goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link in a down clue: the pieces simply stack.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the Greek goddess of wisdom and war, patron of Athens.

clue.text: Pawn ring put on by husband

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter o
to put on a play is to stage it

explanation.surface: A pawned ring is redeemed by a husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pawn' looks like a verb about pledging the ring; it is the noun for a captive used as a bargaining chip.
explanation.definitionFit: A captive held as a bargaining chip is a pawn in someone else's game.

clue.text: Hard hat accordingly put on

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece is placed on top of the second

parts.note: so means therefore or accordingly
lid is slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A hard hat is duly put on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard hat' reads as one item but splits: 'Hard' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something firm and rigid, not liquid or hollow, is described with that adjective.

clue.text: Move to stop explosive missile

indicators.note: a stopper is put inside an opening, so one piece plugs the middle of the other

parts.note: TNT is the abbreviation for the explosive trinitrotoluene
to ride is to move along, as on a horse or in a vehicle

explanation.surface: An order to move to halt an explosive missile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to stop' works like a cork plugging a bottle: the move word is the plug, pushed into the middle of the explosive's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Trident is the name of the submarine-launched ballistic missile carried by British and US navies.

clue.text: Galley: new timer about to be installed

indicators.note: installed means placed within, so one piece is fitted inside the other
new tells us the letters of the word timer are made into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
re is Latin for about or concerning

explanation.surface: A galley gets a new timer fitted shortly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' makes TRIME from the timer's letters; 'to be installed' then fits the Latin word for about into that jumble. 'Galley' suggests a kitchen, but it is the ancient ship.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient warship rowed with three banks of oars is a kind of galley.

clue.text: Historical object Roman Catholic priest locked inside

indicators.note: locked inside means shut within, so one piece sits in the middle of the other

parts.note: Eli is the Old Testament priest who raised Samuel, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A historic object is found with a Catholic priest shut inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: ELI, the biblical priest, sits between R and C.
explanation.definitionFit: A surviving object from the past, or a saint's remains kept for veneration, is called this.

clue.text: Bearer of fruit to relieve badly off

indicators.note: badly off suggests letters in poor shape, so they are reworked into another order

explanation.surface: A charitable plea to help the poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly off' reads as poor people needing relief; it is the signal to rearrange TO RELIEVE.
explanation.definitionFit: That tree is the plant that produces olives, so it is a fruit bearer.

clue.text: Having arrived in Cardiff, earl condemned famous university building

indicators.note: in here places one piece inside the jumbled letters of the other
condemned suggests something ruined or broken up, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

parts.note: came means arrived, past tense

explanation.surface: A nobleman arriving in the Welsh capital is sentenced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'condemned' jumbles the city and the peer into RADCLIFFERA; 'in' fits the arrival word into that jumble. The comma makes 'Having arrived' look like scene-setting.
explanation.definitionFit: This domed library reading room is a celebrated landmark of Oxford University.

clue.text: Consumer after small women's knitted garment

indicators.note: after means the consumer word comes behind the two short letters

parts.note: s is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
w is the abbreviation for women, as on toilet doors
an eater is one who consumes food

explanation.surface: A shopper browsing small women's knitwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small' and 'women's' look like clothing-size words; they are S and W.
explanation.definitionFit: A jumper, knitted from wool, is the garment pulled over the head.

clue.text: Still good, getting hold of Nadal's first service

indicators.note: getting hold of means grabbing and enclosing, so the outer pieces wrap around the letter

parts.note: even so means still or nevertheless

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of the tennis player's name

explanation.surface: A tennis report: the player's first serve is still good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' is not EVEN alone but EVEN SO; 'getting hold of' puts N, the first letter of Nadal, between O and G.
explanation.definitionFit: An evening church service in the Anglican tradition is called by this name.

clue.text: Prize method of learning involving group

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: rote is learning by repetition
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A prize-winning teaching method based on group work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' means the learning method wraps around the group word; learning by rote is learning by sheer repetition.
explanation.definitionFit: A ribbon rosette is awarded as a prize at shows and competitions.

clue.text: Perhaps Vespasian's mood heading off with enlisted men

definitions.note: a single example ruler stands for the class, so 'Perhaps' marks an example

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is cut away from the word

parts.note: a temper is a mood, as in a good or bad temper
OR stands for other ranks, the enlisted men of the army

explanation.surface: A Roman ruler's mood as he sets off with his soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'. 'heading off' takes the first letter from TEMPER, leaving EMPER.
explanation.definitionFit: Vespasian ruled Rome from AD 69 to 79, an example of a Roman sovereign of that title.

clue.text: Travel document and free ticket left

parts.note: a pass is a ticket allowing free entry
port is the left-hand side of a ship

explanation.surface: A traveller's papers and a complimentary ticket left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like a verb (abandoned); it is the nautical side.
explanation.definitionFit: The official identity booklet needed to cross borders is the obvious travel document.

clue.text: Mount charge again

parts.note: to rush is to charge forward
more means additionally, once again

explanation.surface: A cavalry order to mount up and charge once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' looks like a verb (get on horseback); it is a mountain's title.
explanation.definitionFit: The South Dakota mountain carved with four presidents' faces is known by this name.

clue.text: Best old radio receiver part installed in most of these

indicators.note: installed in means fitted inside, so one piece goes within the other
most of means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before trimming
a cat's whisker is the fine wire contact in an early crystal radio set

explanation.surface: A collector praising old radio parts fitted into sets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims the last word to THES; 'installed in' fits the radio part inside it. Early crystal sets tuned in with a fine wire touching the crystal, called by this feline name.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means the finest thing around, an informal superlative like the bee's knees.

clue.text: Involuntary movement made by tense member of coven

parts.note: t is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
a coven is a gathering of witches

explanation.surface: A nervous coven member's spasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tense' looks like an adjective about nerves; it is the grammar term, T.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden jerk or spasm of a muscle is an involuntary movement.

clue.text: Approach a concert's chosen location?

parts.note: a venue is the place where an event such as a concert is held

explanation.surface: How to get to the chosen venue for a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Approach' is a noun: a way or route towards something.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad road or way leading to a place, or a line of attack on a problem, both fit.

clue.text: Walpole, say, in House, ahead of competition

indicators.note: ahead of means the first piece comes before the second

parts.note: a race is a competition

explanation.surface: A politician named Walpole in the House, preparing for an election contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Walpole' suggests Robert Walpole, Britain's first prime minister, and the House of Commons; it is his son, the writer Horace Walpole.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gothic novelist Horace Walpole bears this first name, so he is an example of it.

clue.text: Clubs in correct order

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: to edit is to correct text
c is the abbreviation for clubs, the card suit

explanation.surface: Golf clubs arranged in the right sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in correct order' reads as a phrase; 'order' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An official decree or proclamation issued by authority is an order.

clue.text: Police officer given power within home precinct

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: within means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a sector is a district or precinct
p is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A police officer gains authority over the local precinct.
explanation.walkthrough: P goes into SECTOR after S.
explanation.definitionFit: A detective inspector is a police rank above sergeant, so this is a police officer.

clue.text: Son cutting proper glass object

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: prim means prudishly proper

explanation.surface: A son cutting a fine piece of glass.
explanation.walkthrough: S cuts PRIM between I and M.
explanation.definitionFit: A transparent triangular block of glass that splits light into colours is a glass object.

clue.text: Disorient prisoner having to integrate

parts.note: con is slang for a convict or prisoner
to fuse is to join together, integrate

explanation.surface: A disoriented prisoner struggling to fit back into society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having to' is a link joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To bewilder someone or leave them muddled is to disorient them.

clue.text: Superintendent to check detailed roster sent over

indicators.note: de-tailed means the last letter is cut off the word

parts.note: to curb is to check or restrain

indicators.note: sent over means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a rota is a roster of duties

explanation.surface: A supervisor checks a detailed duty roster sent across.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' looks like it means thorough, but read it as de-tailed: the restraining word loses its last letter. 'sent over' means the duty list is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A keeper in charge of a museum or gallery collection superintends it.
